title: Lesson 6: Worship and the Glory of God
description: Moses saw God's glory, worshiped, and came down the mountain with a face that shone. This lesson walks the whole story: created in God's image to reflect His glory, falling short, pursued and saved through Jesus, and now, with unveiled faces, sent to point others to Him.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, you learned to trust God in the hard places. This lesson lifts your eyes. Before you can understand worship, you need to see the One who is worthy of it, and it begins with a man who asked to see God's glory.

blocks.alt: Moses coming down Mount Sinai with the stone tablets, his face shining so brightly the whole scene is washed in light, then lowering a veil over his face so the mountain path and the camp below come into view

blocks.title: Reflecting God
blocks.text:
While Moses was on Mount Sinai receiving God's law, the people below grew tired of waiting. They melted their gold into a calf and bowed down to it. Moses pleaded with God for them, and then he asked for something bold:

"Please show me your glory." (Exodus 33:18)

God placed Moses in a cleft of the rock and covered him with His hand while His glory passed by. As He passed, God proclaimed His own name, to people who had just broken His heart:

"The LORD, the LORD, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness..." And Moses quickly bowed his head toward the earth and worshiped. (Exodus 34:6, 8)

Then Moses came down the mountain, and something had happened that he did not even know about. "Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone because he had been talking with God" (Exodus 34:29). The people saw it and were afraid to come near, so Moses put a veil over his face. Whenever he went back in to speak with the LORD, he took the veil off.

The light on Moses' face was not his own. It was the reflection of God.

Centuries later, Paul looked back at that veil and saw something better. The glow on Moses' face faded, and he had to cover it. But everyone who belongs to Jesus stands before God with nothing covering their face:
We all, with unveiled faces, are looking as in a mirror at the glory of the Lord and are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory; this is from the Lord who is the Spirit.

Moses saw God's glory, bowed in worship, and carried that glory back to the people on his face. Moses' glow faded, but as you look to the Lord, His Spirit keeps changing you to reflect Him more and more. That is the whole story of worship in one picture, and it is your story too.
6.1 - What fills you with the most awe when you think of God?
What Is God's Glory?

God's glory is the greatness and beauty of who He is, all His perfect qualities shining together: His holiness, power, wisdom, justice, faithfulness, goodness, and love. When Moses asked to see it, God showed him His goodness and told him His name. Creation gives you glimpses of it every day.
The heavens declare the glory of God, and the sky above proclaims his handiwork.
Why You Were Made
The Bible tells one story about God's glory, and you are in it.

Made to reflect Him. God created people in His own image (Genesis 1:27). The moon has no light of its own, but it shines by reflecting the sun. You were made to reflect God's glory in the same way. God calls His people those "whom I created for my glory" (Isaiah 43:7).

Falling short. But people turned away. At Mount Sinai, Israel "exchanged the glory of God for the image of an ox that eats grass" (Psalm 106:20), and every heart does the same in its own way. "All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God" (Romans 3:23). The mirror turned away from the light.

Pursued by God. God did not leave it there. He came after His people, and He sent His Son. Jesus showed the Father's glory perfectly. "We have seen his glory... full of grace and truth" (John 1:14). On the night before the cross, He prayed, "I glorified you on earth, having accomplished the work that you gave me to do" (John 17:4). At the cross you see all of God's glory at once: a God holy enough to judge sin and loving enough to take that judgment Himself. The most amazing thing about God is not only how great He is, but that a God this great loves sinners like you.

Saved to shine. You studied this in Growing Deep: you are saved by grace through faith, and "we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works" (Ephesians 2:10). God saved you to turn you back toward the light, so your life reflects Him again. That is why Jesus could say this:
In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father who is in heaven.
Your good works are not meant to make people admire you. They are meant to make people look up and see your Father.
6.2 - How does knowing you were made to reflect God's glory change the way you see your life?
Worship Is a Response

No one had to teach you to jump out of your seat when your team scored the winning point. You saw something amazing, and you responded. Worship works the same way. It is not a feeling you work up. It is your whole-hearted response to seeing how glorious God is.

And God is not looking for grudging praise. He is honored most when He is your greatest joy. "In your presence there is fullness of joy" (Psalm 16:11). That is why the church sings together. Many voices, one set of words, and the Holy Spirit uniting very different people around one great God (Colossians 3:16). On the weeks your own faith runs low, other voices carry the song. Those are sweet times. Love them, and show up for them.
Until the Whole Earth Sees
You cannot add one ounce of beauty to God. When the Bible tells you to magnify Him, it means helping others see how great He already is.
Oh, magnify the LORD with me, and let us exalt his name together!

A telescope does not make a star bigger. From far away the star looks like a tiny speck, and a telescope shows it as big as it really is. Many people around you think God is small. Your life of worship lifts Him up so they can see Him as He is.

That is why the gospel goes to the nations. As John Piper put it, "Missions exists because worship doesn't." There are still people and places that have never seen how glorious God is, and God has promised that "the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD as the waters cover the sea" (Habakkuk 2:14). Worship and mission belong together. You see His glory, and you point others to it.
6.3 - What are a couple areas in your life that you could reflect God's glory more clearly?
This Week's Practice

Each day this week, write down one glimpse of God's glory you see, in creation, in Scripture, or in something He has done for you, and thank Him for it. Then go sing with your church family this Sunday.
Lesson 6 Review

Moses asked to see God's glory, worshiped, and came down the mountain with a face that shone. You were made to reflect that glory. Everyone has fallen short of it, but God pursued you and sent Jesus, who glorified the Father and saved you by grace. Now you are created in Christ for good works that point others to your Father. Worship is seeing how glorious God is and pointing your whole life toward Him, in song with His people, in your everyday life, and all the way to the nations.
In the next lesson, you will see how worship reaches all the way into your wallet.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?

retiredQuestions.text: 6.1 - What would it look like for you to worship God in a hard place, not because things are good but because He is?
6.2 - How would you explain to a friend what worship is?
6.3 - When have you seen God so clearly that it changed what you did next?
6.4 - Looking at an ordinary week, what does your life say you value most?
6.5 - What has the gathered church given you that you could not have gotten on your own?
6.3 - Who in your life thinks God is small, and how could your life help them see Him as He really is?
